questions.question: How do you implement enterprise SSO (SAML and OIDC) in a Spring Boot app, and what are the common pitfalls?
questions.title: Enterprise SSO: SAML 2.0 and OIDC Integration
questions.direct_answer: For SSO in Spring Boot you pick between **OIDC** (`spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client`) — modern JSON-based, mobile-friendly — and **SAML 2.0** (`spring-security-saml2-service-provider`) — XML-based, required by many enterprise IdPs. Both follow the same conceptual flow: **redirect to IdP -> authenticate -> signed assertion/token returned -> app validates and creates local session**. Configuration involves registering with the IdP (client ID/secret for OIDC; metadata XML + signing keys for SAML), mapping IdP claims/attributes to roles, **JIT user provisioning**, and **Single Logout (SLO)**. Common pitfalls: **redirect URI mismatch**, **signature validation**, **clock skew**, **claim mapping**, **cert rotation**. **Modern B2B default**: OIDC primary, SAML fallback for enterprise mandate.

interviewer_intent.testing: Understanding of enterprise SSO flows, SAML vs OIDC trade-offs, JIT provisioning, SLO
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Treating SSO as one protocol; missing signature/cert validation; not handling cert rotation
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss multi-tenant SSO, dynamic registration, JIT provisioning, SLO complexity, Azure AD / Okta specifics

sections.title: Enterprise SSO Landscape
sections.content:
**Enterprise SSO**: user logs into central IdP once, gains access to many apps without re-authenticating. Two protocols dominate.

**OIDC (OpenID Connect)** — OAuth2 + identity layer. JSON tokens (JWT ID + access). Modern, mobile-friendly, smaller messages. Supported by Okta, Auth0, Azure AD, Google Workspace, AWS Cognito, Keycloak.

**SAML 2.0** — XML assertions signed by IdP. Older (2005) but **entrenched in enterprise**. ADFS, Azure AD (SAML mode), Okta, Ping, Shibboleth. Required by banks, governments, healthcare, large corporates.

**Spring Boot starters:**
- **OIDC**: `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client` (login initiation + token handling)
- **SAML**: `spring-security-saml2-service-provider` (as Service Provider)

**Choosing:**
- **OIDC first** if IdP supports it (Okta, Auth0, Azure AD, Cognito all do)
- **SAML** if customer mandates or IdP is SAML-only (legacy ADFS, government)
- **Both** if you sell B2B SaaS — different customers, different IdPs

sections.title: SAML 2.0 SP-Initiated SSO Flow
sections.content:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "User Browser"
    participant SP as "Service Provider (Spring Boot app)"
    participant IdP as "Identity Provider (Okta, ADFS, Azure AD)"

    User->>SP: "GET /protected (no session)"
    SP->>SP: "Build AuthnRequest XML, generate RelayState (random opaque value)"
    SP-->>User: "302 redirect to IdP SSO URL with SAMLRequest base64 deflated and RelayState"
    User->>IdP: "GET /sso/saml with SAMLRequest and RelayState"
    IdP->>User: "Login form (or SSO if existing IdP session)"
    User->>IdP: "Submit credentials and MFA"
    IdP->>IdP: "Build SAMLResponse with signed Assertion (XML signature, NotBefore NotOnOrAfter, AudienceRestriction, AttributeStatement)"
    IdP-->>User: "HTML auto-POST form to SP ACS URL with SAMLResponse and RelayState"
    User->>SP: "POST /login/saml2/sso/registrationId with SAMLResponse and RelayState"
    SP->>SP: "Verify XML signature with IdP cert, check Issuer Audience NotBefore NotOnOrAfter, validate InResponseTo matches AuthnRequest, parse AttributeStatement"
    SP->>SP: "Map attributes to authorities (groups -> ROLE_*), JIT provision user if first login"
    SP->>SP: "Create local HTTP session, store SecurityContext"
    SP-->>User: "302 redirect to original RelayState target (/protected)"
    User->>SP: "GET /protected with JSESSIONID cookie"
    SP-->>User: "200 protected resource"
```

sections.title: OIDC Configuration in Spring Boot
SAML 2.0 Configuration
Multi-Tenant SSO and Common Patterns
sections.content:
**B2B SaaS with per-customer IdP — resolve tenant from subdomain or email domain, route to right registration:**

```java
@Bean
InMemoryClientRegistrationRepository clientRegs(ClientRegistrationLoader loader) {
    return new InMemoryClientRegistrationRepository(loader.loadAll());
}

@Bean
SecurityFilterChain chain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    return http
        .oauth2Login(o -> o.loginPage("/login/tenant"))
        .build();
}
```

**For dynamic / many tenants** — implement custom `ClientRegistrationRepository` that reads from DB.

**SAML multi-tenant:** custom `RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository` sourced from DB, keyed by tenant.

**User attribute mapping contract — agree per IdP:**
- **User identifier** — `email` or `sub`
- **Display name** — `name`, `givenName`+`familyName`, `displayName`
- **Role/group** — varies (`groups`, `roles`, `memberOf`); map named groups to internal roles
- **Custom claims** — department, tenant, etc.

**Single Logout (SLO):**
- **OIDC** — `OidcClientInitiatedLogoutSuccessHandler` redirects to IdP's `end_session_endpoint`
- **SAML** — `saml2Logout()` handles SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SLO
- Both: app destroys local session; IdP signs out user from other apps

**JIT provisioning rules:**
- First login: create local user with IdP-provided attributes
- Subsequent logins: update attributes if changed
- Conflicts: existing local user with same email + different subject ID
- Use **federated ID (issuer + subject)** as primary key, not just email

**Session semantics:**
- After SSO: local HTTP session (if MVC)
- SSO = one-time auth; session lifetime is yours
- Re-authenticate with IdP periodically (silent renewal) or require re-login after X hours

**Combining SSO with local accounts:**
- Some users SSO; others local password
- Multiple `AuthenticationProvider`s
- Common pattern: SSO-only for enterprise; local for freemium

sections.title: Pitfalls, Security, Testing, Observability
sections.content:
**When OIDC helps:**
- Mobile + SPA support out of the box
- JSON tokens, smaller messages
- PKCE, refresh rotation standard
- Modern IdPs all support it

**When SAML is required:**
- Enterprise customer mandate
- Legacy ADFS, government, healthcare
- Established compliance frameworks expect SAML

**When it hurts:**
- Hand-parsing XML in SAML -> signature wrapping attacks
- Missing PKCE for public clients -> code interception
- Email-as-identifier -> user identity loss when emails change
- Hard-coded certs without rotation -> auth breaks at cert expiry

**Watch for (common pitfalls):**
- **Redirect URI mismatch** — exact scheme/host/port/path; trust `X-Forwarded-Proto` behind LB
- **Clock skew** — SAML `NotBefore`/`NotOnOrAfter`, JWT `nbf`/`exp`; NTP + tolerance
- **Signature validation failure** — wrong cert/algorithm/expired; check logs; rotate proactively
- **Cert rotation** — `metadata-uri` where possible; multiple `verification.credentials`
- **Claim mapping confusion** — version contract; log available claims in dev
- **Missing PKCE on public clients** — mobile/SPA must use
- **XML signature wrapping (SAML)** — use Spring's library; never hand-parse XML
- **Missing `state` (OIDC)** — CSRF during callback; Spring auto-generates; don't disable
- **Logout local-only** — user re-authenticates with one click; implement SLO for compliance
- **Email as identifier** — emails change; use federated ID (issuer+subject)
- **`SameSite=Strict` cookie** — breaks SSO callback POST; use `Lax` or `None+Secure`
- **IdP-initiated SSO without `RelayState`** — app doesn't know where to land; SP-initiated preferred

**Testing:**
- Unit test claim mapping with mock `OidcUser` / `Saml2AuthenticatedPrincipal`
- Integration with Keycloak Testcontainers (real OIDC flow)
- SAML: Keycloak in SAML mode or Shibboleth
- Contract tests with IdP team on claim schema

**Observability:**
- Log `AuthenticationSuccessEvent`, `AbstractAuthenticationFailureEvent`
- Log failed cert validation, assertion expiration
- Metric: `auth.attempts{result, reason}`
- Alert on failure spikes (IdP outage, cert expired)
- Audit trail (who, when, where, IdP) for compliance

**Security hardening:**
- HTTPS only + HSTS
- `SameSite=Lax` cookies (or `None+Secure` for cross-domain)
- Content Security Policy
- Session ID rotation on login (fixation defense)
- Idle + absolute session timeout
- Rate-limit login attempts at SP layer

**Debug tips:**
- `logging.level.org.springframework.security=DEBUG`
- SAML tracer browser extension (Firefox)
- oauthdebugger.com for OIDC URL generation
- Keycloak local as generic IdP for dev

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **OIDC vs SAML** — OIDC modern JSON (mobile-friendly); SAML XML enterprise (legacy, still required).
- **Spring Boot OIDC** — `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client` + `oauth2Login()` DSL.
- **Spring Boot SAML** — `spring-security-saml2-service-provider` + `saml2Login()` DSL.
- **PKCE** for public clients in OIDC; automatic in Spring Security 6.
- **JIT provisioning** on first login; map IdP claims to local user + roles.
- **Single Logout (SLO)** for compliance — OIDC `end_session_endpoint`, SAML SLO.
- **Multi-tenant SSO** — custom `ClientRegistrationRepository` / `RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository` sourced from DB.
- **Cert rotation** — `metadata-uri` where possible; maintain multiple `verification.credentials`.
- **Pitfalls** — redirect URI, clock skew, signature errors, claim mapping, `SameSite` cookies.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**OIDC vs SAML quick framing**
- OIDC: modern JSON-based, mobile-friendly, primary choice for new integrations
- SAML: XML-based, enterprise-required (banks, gov, healthcare); fallback for B2B
- Both: redirect to IdP -> auth -> signed response -> local session

**OIDC in Spring Boot**
- `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client`
- `application.yml`: `spring.security.oauth2.client.registration.<id>` + `provider.<id>.issuer-uri`
- `oauth2Login(...)` DSL, `userInfoEndpoint.userAuthoritiesMapper` for role mapping
- `OidcClientInitiatedLogoutSuccessHandler` for SLO
- `@AuthenticationPrincipal OidcUser` in controllers
- PKCE automatic with `client-authentication-method=none`

**SAML 2.0 in Spring Boot**
- `spring-security-saml2-service-provider`
- `spring.security.saml2.relyingparty.registration.<id>` with `assertingparty.metadata-uri`
- `saml2Login()` and `saml2Logout()` DSL
- `OpenSaml4AuthenticationProvider` with `setResponseAuthenticationConverter` for attribute mapping
- Cert rotation via multiple `verification.credentials`

**Multi-tenant**
- Resolve tenant from subdomain or email domain
- Custom repository sourced from DB

**JIT provisioning**
- First login -> create local user from IdP attributes
- Use federated ID (issuer + subject), not just email

**Common pitfalls**
- Redirect URI mismatch (exact match required)
- Clock skew on assertion validity
- Cert rotation breaking auth
- Claim mapping silently dropping roles
- SameSite=Strict breaking callback POST
- Logout only local without SLO -> one-click re-login

**2026 default**
- OIDC primary, SAML on enterprise request
- Use IdP aggregator (Auth0, WorkOS) for many customer IdPs

questions.question: How do you decide between SAML and OIDC, and how do you wire up Spring Security's saml2 RelyingPartyRegistration end-to-end?
questions.title: SAML vs OIDC Decision and Spring Security saml2 RelyingPartyRegistration
questions.direct_answer: **Decision rule**: prefer **OIDC** for new integrations (modern JSON, PKCE, mobile/SPA support); choose **SAML** when the customer's IdP only speaks SAML or compliance/procurement mandates it. In Spring Security 6, SAML 2.0 SP support is built into **`spring-security-saml2-service-provider`** and centers on **`RelyingPartyRegistration`** — it holds the SP entity ID, the ACS (assertion consumer) and SLO URLs, the SP signing/decryption keys, and the **`AssertingPartyDetails`** (IdP entity ID, SSO/SLO URLs, verification certs). You enable it with **`http.saml2Login()`** and **`http.saml2Logout()`**, store registrations in a **`RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository`** (in-memory or DB-backed for multi-tenant), and customize attribute-to-authority mapping via **`OpenSaml4AuthenticationProvider.setResponseAuthenticationConverter`**.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the candidate can both reason about protocol choice and walk through the SP-side wiring in Spring Security 6.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Treating SAML as legacy and ignoring it; or wiring SAML without understanding RelyingPartyRegistration, ACS URL, or signature verification.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss DB-backed RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository for multi-tenant, encrypted assertions, NameID format selection, and the OpenSAML4 customization hook.

sections.title: When to Choose SAML vs OIDC
sections.content:
**OIDC and SAML solve the same problem** — federated authentication — but they're shaped by different eras.
- **OIDC**
- is OAuth2 + identity layer with JSON tokens; small messages, mobile-friendly, simple JWKS for keys, automatic PKCE for public clients.
- **SAML 2.0**.
- is XML assertions signed and optionally encrypted with X.509 certs; verbose, browser-only (no native mobile flow), but **deeply entrenched in enterprise**.

**Default rule:** prefer OIDC for new integrations; fall back to SAML when customer requires it. In B2B SaaS, support both — large enterprise tenants will mandate SAML even when OIDC is available, often for compliance / procurement reasons rather than technical ones.

**Spring Security 6 makes both first-class:**
- **OIDC** via `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client` and `http.oauth2Login()`
- **SAML 2.0** via `spring-security-saml2-service-provider` and `http.saml2Login()`

The SAML side centers on **`RelyingPartyRegistration`** — a single immutable object describing one SP-IdP relationship. For multi-tenant apps, you have many registrations and resolve at runtime via the registration ID embedded in the URL (`/login/saml2/sso/{registrationId}`).

sections.title: SAML vs OIDC: Decision Matrix
sections.content:
Use this table to drive the choice in interviews and design docs.

| Aspect | SAML 2.0 | OIDC |
|---|---|---|
| **Era / wire format** | 2005, XML, signed + optionally encrypted | 2014, JSON (JWT), signed |
| **Token size** | KB-sized assertions | Compact JWTs (~1-2 KB) |
| **Mobile / native apps** | Awkward (browser POST) | First-class (PKCE) |
| **SPA support** | Possible but ugly | First-class with PKCE |
| **Discovery** | XML metadata | `.well-known/openid-configuration` |
| **Key rotation** | X.509 cert rotation, manual or via metadata refresh | JWKS endpoint, automatic |
| **Encryption** | Encrypted assertions standard | Tokens not normally encrypted (TLS for transport) |
| **Standard library** | OpenSAML, Spring Security saml2 | Many; Spring Security oauth2-client |
| **Common IdPs** | ADFS, Azure AD (SAML mode), Okta, Ping, Shibboleth | Okta, Auth0, Azure AD (OIDC mode), Google, Cognito, Keycloak |
| **Use SAML when** | Customer mandate, legacy ADFS, gov/healthcare | Rarely the right new choice |
| **Use OIDC when** | New integrations, mobile/SPA, modern IdP | Default for greenfield |

**Rule of thumb:**
- **Greenfield + you control IdP** -> OIDC
- **B2B SaaS, customer brings IdP** -> support both; OIDC primary
- **Compliance-bound (HIPAA, FedRAMP) or government** -> SAML often required
- **Mobile-first** -> OIDC + PKCE, SAML is painful

sections.title: RelyingPartyRegistration Anatomy
sections.content:
**A `RelyingPartyRegistration` carries everything Spring needs to talk to one IdP:**

```java
RelyingPartyRegistration registration = RelyingPartyRegistrations
    .fromMetadataLocation("https://idp.example.com/metadata")
    .registrationId("okta")
    .entityId("{baseUrl}/saml2/service-provider-metadata/{registrationId}")
    .assertionConsumerServiceLocation("{baseUrl}/login/saml2/sso/{registrationId}")
    .singleLogoutServiceLocation("{baseUrl}/logout/saml2/slo")
    .signingX509Credentials(c -> c.add(spSigningCredential()))
    .decryptionX509Credentials(c -> c.add(spDecryptionCredential()))
    .build();
```

**The pieces, explained:**
- **`registrationId`** — opaque ID embedded in URLs (`/login/saml2/sso/<registrationId>`); chooses which registration handles the response
- **`entityId`** — the SP's SAML identity; placed in `<saml2:Issuer>` of `AuthnRequest`
- **`assertionConsumerServiceLocation` (ACS)** — where IdP POSTs the SAMLResponse; must match what's registered with IdP
- **`singleLogoutServiceLocation`** — endpoint for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SLO
- **`signingX509Credentials`** — SP private key + cert for signing AuthnRequest and LogoutRequest
- **`decryptionX509Credentials`** — SP private key for decrypting encrypted assertions
- **`AssertingPartyDetails`** (loaded from IdP metadata) — IdP entity ID, SSO/SLO URLs, verification certs

**Property-driven equivalent (Spring Boot):**

```yaml
spring:
  security:
    saml2:
      relyingparty:
        registration:
          okta:
            entity-id: "{baseUrl}/saml2/service-provider-metadata/{registrationId}"
            signing:
              credentials:
                - private-key-location: classpath:sp.key
                  certificate-location: classpath:sp.cert
            decryption:
              credentials:
                - private-key-location: classpath:sp.key
                  certificate-location: classpath:sp.cert
            assertingparty:
              metadata-uri: https://idp.example.com/metadata
```

**Spring Boot auto-creates a `RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository`** from these properties.

**SP metadata exposed automatically:**
- `GET /saml2/service-provider-metadata/{registrationId}` returns XML metadata for the SP
- Hand this to your IdP admin to register the SP — no manual XML authoring

sections.title: Wiring saml2Login, saml2Logout, and Custom Auth Mapping
Multi-Tenant SAML and DB-Backed Registrations
sections.content:
**For B2B SaaS with many customer IdPs, you cannot list every IdP in `application.yml`. Implement a custom repository.**

**DB-backed `RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository`:**

```java
@Component
public class TenantRelyingPartyRegistrationRepository
        implements RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository {

    private final TenantRepository tenantRepo;
    private final ConcurrentMap<String, RelyingPartyRegistration> cache =
        new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    @Override
    public RelyingPartyRegistration findByRegistrationId(String registrationId) {
        return cache.computeIfAbsent(registrationId, id ->
            tenantRepo.findByRegistrationId(id)
                .map(this::buildRegistration)
                .orElse(null));
    }

    private RelyingPartyRegistration buildRegistration(TenantConfig t) {
        return RelyingPartyRegistrations
            .fromMetadataLocation(t.idpMetadataUri())
            .registrationId(t.registrationId())
            .entityId("{baseUrl}/saml2/service-provider-metadata/{registrationId}")
            .assertionConsumerServiceLocation(
                "{baseUrl}/login/saml2/sso/{registrationId}")
            .signingX509Credentials(c -> c.add(spSigningCredential()))
            .decryptionX509Credentials(c -> c.add(spDecryptionCredential()))
            .build();
    }
}
```

**Tenant resolution — three common patterns:**
- **Subdomain**: `acme.app.com` -> registrationId `acme`
- **Email domain**: user enters email; lookup `tenant_domains` table; redirect to right registrationId
- **Tenant query param**: `/login?tenant=acme` -> redirect to `/saml2/authenticate/acme`

**Cache invalidation on tenant config changes:**
- Refresh endpoint that calls `cache.invalidate(registrationId)`
- Or short TTL + lazy refresh on next request

**Encrypted assertions:**
- Some IdPs encrypt the entire assertion (additional confidentiality on top of TLS)
- SP needs `decryptionX509Credentials` configured
- `OpenSaml4AuthenticationProvider` decrypts automatically if credentials are present

**NameID format selection (less common, IdP-specific):**
- `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress` — most common
- `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent` — opaque stable ID
- Configure on `AssertingPartyDetails` if IdP requires explicit format

**Production checklist:**
- Use `metadata-uri` so cert rotations propagate automatically
- Multiple `verification.credentials` during cert rotation windows
- Encrypted assertions for PHI/PII data flows
- Federated ID = `(issuer, NameID)` as user primary key, not email
- SP-initiated SSO over IdP-initiated when possible (RelayState carries return URL)

sections.title: SAML in Spring: Helps, Hurts, Watch For
sections.content:
**When Spring Security saml2 helps:**
- First-class SAML 2.0 SP without OpenSAML boilerplate
- Auto-generated SP metadata endpoint
- Built-in SLO and SP-initiated SSO
- Property-driven config for simple cases; programmatic for multi-tenant

**When SAML hurts overall:**
- XML wire format is verbose; payloads can exceed 50 KB
- Browser-POST binding makes mobile/native UX awkward
- Cert rotation is a recurring operational task
- IdP-initiated SSO without RelayState leaves no return URL

**Watch for:**
- **ACS URL mismatch** — must be exactly what's registered with IdP (scheme, host, port, path)
- **Behind load balancer** — set `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework` so `{baseUrl}` reflects external URL
- **Clock skew** — `NotBefore`/`NotOnOrAfter` reject with seconds of drift; sync NTP
- **Cert expiry** — IdP cert silently rotated; signature validation breaks; alerts on expiry windows
- **Encrypted assertions** — SP decryption credential mandatory; missing -> assertion unreadable
- **`@AuthenticationPrincipal` type confusion** — use `Saml2AuthenticatedPrincipal`, not OIDC `OidcUser`
- **Email change** — using email as primary key breaks identity continuity; use federated ID `(issuer, NameID)`
- **`SameSite=Strict` cookie** — breaks IdP POST callback; use `Lax`
- **Hand-parsed XML** — signature wrapping attacks; always use Spring's library
- **Single registration in `application.yml`** — fine for one IdP; explodes at multi-tenant scale; switch to DB-backed repo early
- **`saml2Logout`** with no IdP-side configuration — local logout works; IdP session persists; one-click re-login

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **Choose OIDC for new integrations**, SAML when customer/IdP requires it.
- **`RelyingPartyRegistration`** is the central object — entity ID, ACS, SLO, SP keys, IdP details.
- **`spring.security.saml2.relyingparty.registration.*`** auto-creates a registration; `assertingparty.metadata-uri` is simplest.
- **`http.saml2Login()` + `saml2Logout()` + `saml2Metadata()`** wires the endpoints (`/login/saml2/sso/{id}`, `/logout/saml2/slo`, `/saml2/service-provider-metadata/{id}`).
- **`OpenSaml4AuthenticationProvider.setResponseAuthenticationConverter`** is where you map SAML attributes to `GrantedAuthority`.
- **Multi-tenant** — implement custom `RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository`; resolve tenant from subdomain/email/query.
- **Cert rotation** — prefer `metadata-uri`; multiple `verification.credentials` during rotation windows.
- **Use federated ID `(issuer, NameID)`** as user primary key; emails change.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**Decision rule**
- OIDC for new integrations: modern JSON, PKCE, mobile-friendly
- SAML when customer mandates it (enterprise, gov, healthcare)
- B2B SaaS: support both; OIDC primary, SAML fallback

**SAML in Spring 6: starter and DSL**
- `spring-security-saml2-service-provider`
- `http.saml2Login()` + `saml2Logout()` + `saml2Metadata()`

**RelyingPartyRegistration anatomy**
- `registrationId` — opaque ID in URLs
- `entityId` — SP's SAML identity
- ACS URL — `/login/saml2/sso/{registrationId}` where IdP POSTs response
- SLO URL — `/logout/saml2/slo`
- SP signing + decryption keys
- AssertingPartyDetails from IdP metadata

**Property-driven config**
- `spring.security.saml2.relyingparty.registration.<id>` with `assertingparty.metadata-uri`
- Spring auto-creates `RelyingPartyRegistrationRepository`
- SP metadata XML at `/saml2/service-provider-metadata/{id}`

**Auto endpoints**
- `GET /saml2/authenticate/{id}` initiates SP-initiated SSO
- `POST /login/saml2/sso/{id}` is the ACS
- `POST /logout/saml2/slo` for SLO

**Custom attribute -> authority**
- `OpenSaml4AuthenticationProvider.setResponseAuthenticationConverter`
- Read `groups` attribute, map to `ROLE_*`

**Multi-tenant**
